kmpwright.boundary: public Kotlin Multiplatform Page, Locator, Browser, and configuration APIs

statusDefinitions.supported: The command's documented core behavior has a public Kmpwright entry point.
statusDefinitions.partial: A public entry point exists, but backend, lifecycle, output, or option semantics differ; callers must handle the documented limitation.
statusDefinitions.unsupported: There is no public Kmpwright entry point for this command or option.

commands.semantics: Inspect persistent bounded request history, stable redirect-hop IDs, request/response detail and on-demand CDP bodies.
commands.notes: Retains at most 500 hops within a 4 MiB metadata budget, across navigations. Native visibility follows WebView SDK event coverage; native response body retrieval explicitly throws unsupported. Evicted/cached/redirect bodies may be unavailable.

commands.semantics: Represent HAR 1.2 records.
commands.notes: Portable HAR 1.2 capture from unified page/frame events; CDP includes available text/base64 bodies, native SDKs expose partial metadata. Bounded entries, byte retention and body reads; truncated bodies are explicit.

commands.semantics: List, switch, and close pages/tabs.
commands.notes: Tabs opened from a page inherit successful headers, credentials, routes, emulation and init scripts before navigating. Independent Browser.newPage/context pages retain their configured ownership. Browser-scoped CDP enumerates existing targets and attaches without taking tab ownership. Activation revives discarded renderers. Attachment close detaches; explicit target close closes the tab.

commands.semantics: Create a separate top-level browser window.
commands.notes: Browser-scoped CDP creates an owned top-level window; native WebViews and page-scoped endpoints reject this explicitly.

commands.semantics: Resolve locators in an iframe.
commands.notes: CDP resolves same-process and nested cross-origin/process frames, routes scoped native input/upload/screenshots/AX roles and refreshes after process swaps. Native WebViews retain same-origin DOM frame limitations.

commands.semantics: Start and stop the V8 CPU profiler.
commands.notes: Only CDP-backed pages support profiling.

commands.semantics: Inspect React fibers, renders, or Suspense boundaries.
commands.notes: React DevTools Inline 8.0.0 with private React 19.3.0 runtime. Typed tree/inspection, render profiles and rich Suspense metadata; DOM renderer selection handles Flight-first registration. Bounded capture, serialized hook operations and cleanup verified with a real React 19.3 application.

commands.notes: Typed CWV metrics/ratings, LCP/CLS details and React profiling hydration/component timing. Bundled web-vitals 6.2.3; observer/listener cleanup verified in real Chrome. Missing observations remain null.

commands.semantics: Save and restore cookies/local storage state.
commands.notes: Explicit restore and page-owned periodic autosave, observable failures, authenticated encryption and atomic file replacement. Daemon summary/session protocols are excluded.

commands.semantics: Isolate or persist browser state across runs.

commands.semantics: Configure browser profile/state storage.
commands.notes: Profile reuse is backend/platform dependent and not a public equivalent of Chrome profile discovery.

commands.semantics: Stream the browser viewport over agent-browser's runtime WebSocket.
commands.notes: Cold CDP JPEG frame flow with independent capture sessions, latest-frame delivery, FPS/quality/size controls and cancellation cleanup. The caller supplies a display or transport; agent-browser dashboard/WebSocket server is excluded. Native WebViews explicitly report unsupported.

commands.semantics: Install, configure, or run agent-browser executable plugins.
Run an axe-core accessibility audit (distinct from a snapshot).
commands.notes: Bundled axe-core 4.14.0 with bounded findings, tags, selector errors and preserved shadow/frame target paths. CDP audits merge isolated frame partials including OOPIFs; native WebViews report skipped child frames explicitly.

commands.semantics: Discover, invoke, cancel, or retrieve experimental page-provided WebMCP tools.
commands.notes: Typed WebMCP catalog/context and invocation/result/cancellation with upstream limits. Observes owned pages before navigation and routes OOPIF tools by session. Real Chrome verifies same-process and cross-process duplicate names and explicit frame invocation. Initial preconnected same-process child tool replay remains a protocol limitation; native WebViews report unavailable.

commands.semantics: Record browser video, cursor overlays, or contact sheets through ffmpeg.
commands.notes: CDP/FFmpeg recording of the current page at fixed 1–60 FPS, clean contact sheets, trusted pointer observation, cursor composition, output preflight and bounded cleanup. Native WebViews cannot expose CDP screencasting.

Owned Linux Chromium uses a temporary NSS HOME and certutil; JVM/Android HTTP readers support per-instance PEM/DER trust. Darwin custom trust is explicitly unsupported. Real HTTPS tests verify private trust and hostname rejection; Linux NSS browser integration requires Linux validation.
Closing the owned browser removes its isolated CA trust store; each HTTP read closes its per-instance client. There is no global CLI CA state to clear.
